summary: The sample construction and denominator fixes are internally consistent, but the machine-B replication workflow does not preflight or hash the new required sample artifact. The MI-match comparison also changes the validator between Old and New, so the generated “Link Quality” tables conflate improved links with re-transcription of the validating initial.

findings.title: The new required sample file is absent from machine-B preflight and input hashing
findings.what_the_code_does: Both table scripts now read `local sample_f "$D_FLAGS/linkage_sample1940.dta"`, but the file is built on machine A and must be manually copied to machine B. The machine-B preflight still checks the superseded `ipums_fs_names_for_Deaglan1940.dta` and old 1940 name files, while `hash_inputs_machineB.py` continues to require exactly 17 inputs parsed from that stale list.
findings.why_it_matters: A preflight can report that every input is present and then the four-hour table run can fail immediately when the first analysis opens the unlisted sample file. Even when manually copied, this result-determining artifact has no manifest hash, so the reported tables cannot be tied to the frozen input set claimed by the replication package.
findings.how_to_check: On machine B, run `confirm file "$D_FLAGS/linkage_sample1940.dta"` and then run `replication/Run-MachineB.ps1 -PreflightOnly`; inspect whether the preflight detects the file's absence. Also run `rg -n "linkage_sample1940" replication/run_machineB.do replication/hash_inputs_machineB.py replication/input_manifest_machineB.md`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `data/names/flags/linkage_sample1940.dta` to `run_machineB.do` preflight and regenerate the machine-B manifest from the revised list. Remove the three superseded inputs if no active table script reads them, update the expected manifest count, and automate or document a checksummed machine-A-to-B transfer rather than relying only on the copy instruction.

findings.title: The Old/New MI-match columns change the validator as well as the links
findings.what_the_code_does: For Old links the code sets `miv` to `mi_anc`, while for New links it sets it to `mi_ml`, then computes `count if mi1930 == mi1940`. The resulting values are printed side by side as `MI Match Rate` under `Panel A: Coverage and Link Quality`, even though both the linked pairs and the 1940 validating initial change.
findings.why_it_matters: An increase in this row cannot be attributed to improved linkage quality: it can arise because the model re-read the middle initial differently even when the linked pair is unchanged. The table caption and row label do not disclose this moving-validator design, so a reader can interpret the difference as independent validation of the links.
findings.how_to_check: Run `replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do`, which already scores both ABE versions against one fixed 1940 initial, and compare its fixed-validator change with the own-initial change. Apply the same fixed-`mi_anc` and fixed-`mi_ml` calculation to the JW and HLINK pairs before retaining their MI rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Either score Old and New links against the same fixed 1940 initial and report that comparison, or relabel and footnote the existing row explicitly as own-transcription agreement. If retained, present the fixed-validator result alongside it so the link-selection contribution is identifiable.

verified_clean.evidence: The artifact reads `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` at LINKAGE/code/prep/build_linkage_sample1940.do:51-52; that dataset's construction filters `namelast`, `namefrst`, `namefrst_fs`, and `namelast_fs` for nonempty values at CODE/clean_FS_and_combineV5_nber.do:225.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so prose claims and disclosure outside the generated table text could not be compared with the code.

The external census, linkage, and truth datasets were unavailable in the repository, and the Stata pipeline could not be run; runtime results and asserted record counts remain source-based inferences.
The review was limited to the uncommitted working-tree changes and directly relevant pipeline controls, not a full audit of all pre-existing linkage code.
The FamilySearch-profile truth set's independence and selection properties could not be empirically assessed without the underlying data and linkage diagnostics.
